content.thinking:
These are reference-implementation bugs: when there are no atoms, the empty-alphabet DFA must still have one row per state with one entry per declared service (transitions exist even if there are no atoms — the DFA is over the full alphabet!). My reference special-cased the no-atoms case to produce `[[]]`, which is wrong: `next` must have one integer per declared service. My main implementation handles it correctly (it builds a product with 0 monitors and generates rows of length alpha pointing to state 0).

Fix ref_compile: remove the special case and instead handle k==0 by building a single-state product with rows of length n all pointing to 0.

Let me patch ref_impl.
